newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Seven inmates tunnel out of Honduran jail.
newsitem.headline: Seven inmates tunnel out of Honduran jail.

text.p: Seven dangerous inmates escaped from a jail by digging a 36-foot (12 meter) tunnel, the prison director said on Wednesday.
The breakout was discovered late on Tuesday in the sultry industrial city of San Pedro Sula, 100 miles (165 km) north of the capital city. The jail holds 1,500 convicts.
Local press dubbed the escape the most spectacular in Honduran history. Authorities ordered a national alert to capture the fugitives and keep them from leaving the country.

"There are seven convicts on the run. They dug a 12-meter tunnel from a carpentry workshop to beyond the outer wall," director Juan Paz said. He said the fugitives, including murderers, drug traffickers and bank robbers, dug the tunnel over a period of weeks using tools from the workshop.
An investigation is under way to find out how they could have dug the tunnel for so long without being caught, he said.
